title: CUDA programming: tools, kernels, and launch configuration
status: reviewed and locally validated; independent round 2 ACCEPT
transcript_provenance: Local machine transcription (faster-whisper small.en); not publisher captions
source_uncertainties: Both assigned transcripts read completely;25 selected frames inspected. No complete independent audio review. The second lecture memory-function slide f0016 was added after the initial24-frame inventory.

The actual lectures present CUDA interfaces and flags but no complete pi/Jacobi implementation. Vector-add protocol, storage test, pi reduction and diagnostic are original teaching constructions. Jacobi appears only as a lifetime/ordering connection, not a reproduced solver.
The current web CUDA guide/API/compiler docs were served as newer13.4 documentation; installed13.3 headers and compiler help establish executable names and flags. No version identity is claimed.

An initial current AMD HIP page returned429, while the explicitly dated6.4.1 porting guide opened successfully. A subsequent deeper open returned429 again; the successful Porting a CUDA Project passage supports the stated NVIDIA-to-AMD workflow. No exhaustive current vendor/package support matrix was validated.

Classic atomicFetchAdd-style names listed on the slide are absent from the nine inspected installed atomic headers and absent from the documented classic family; the chapter does not claim that newer __nv_atomic_fetch_add or other atomic interfaces do not exist.

cudaErrorOutOfMemory is absent from the installed runtime enum, while cudaErrorMemoryAllocation is present. cudaErrorPriorLaunchFailure and cudaErrorInvalidDevicePointer are retained with deprecation comments; the chapter does not present them as modern diagnostic recommendations.

The safe negative example requests maxThreadsPerBlock+1 and recognizes only cudaErrorInvalidConfiguration or the actually observed cudaErrorInvalidValue as recoverable submission rejections. It does not execute an invalid memory access, divergent barrier, deliberate watchdog timeout or a hang. No general fault-recovery guarantee is inferred from clearing last-error state.

Floating reduction checks compare every block partial and total with a long-double numerical reference and use5e-12 floating allowance plus exact-arithmetic quadrature bound. This tolerance is validated for listed cases, not proved universal rounding accuracy. No bitwise serial/GPU identity is demanded.

Vector/type example exact comparisons are justified by bounded binary-exact input values. Float3 representation and dim3 defaults are checked on installed ABI; grouping values alone establishes neither SIMD instructions nor coalescing.

Four captures were serialized in the exclusive slot. Each printed kernel time is one event interval, not a steady-state minimum-of-many benchmark. Power/clocks/background services are uncontrolled; observed ranges are not confidence intervals.

The allocation-to-free host interval includes transfers, allocations and API overhead, but excludes device initialization/query, input/reference construction and post-copy validation. Vector output initialization deliberately adds a diagnostic host-to-device copy. No device-memory/link peak or whole-application speedup is inferred.

ComputeSanitizer/Nsight table describes possible diagnostic scopes from primary tool manuals. Those tools were not executed and no profiler/sanitizer finding is claimed. No installation or global configuration change was performed.

The initial diagnostic expected only InvalidConfiguration and exited2 on actual InvalidValue. Its raw failure, source snapshot and two repair stages are retained. Final program validates a healthy baseline, resets the output, recognizes the bounded rejection, clears error bookkeeping and validates a fresh legal result. No cause for enum variation was isolated. Observed stack runtime13030/driverAPI13010/driverpackage592.82; no identical enum across all versions is promised.

Cold first-launch event intervals ranged607.104-15837.184us for one addition. The output field kernel_us is explicitly interpreted as elapsed time between event markers, possibly including device-idle submission gaps, not isolated GPU busy time/arithmetic latency. Runtime/startup/scheduling cause was not isolated.
The final parsed checker reran complete contracts separately and passed all four; its variable timing output is excluded from the four-capture ranges.
lecture_corrections: HIP portability qualified by actual AMD6.4.1 porting guide
vector grouping does not automatically coalesce accesses or produce SIMD operations
classic atomicAdd returns old; atomicFetchAdd-style names not present in installed atomic headers
runtime versus driver query names/enums must not be mixed
cudaErrorOutOfMemory absent from runtime enum; cudaErrorMemoryAllocation correct, old names deprecated
nvcc -g host versus -G device; device optimization defaults rather than interpreting -Ohost as device unoptimized
The second launch slide declares myKernel but uses kernel in its invocation; name and signature must match.
dim3 omitted components default1; dimension counts multiply, while thread/block indices are zero-based.
An event host wait represents completion of captured stream work, not a new all-thread rendezvous; host device synchronization does not replace an in-kernel block barrier.
Classic atomics protect one read-modify-write at their scope, not arbitrary surrounding code, a deterministic thread order or one update per clock.
